title: Realistic daylight room
goal: Make the room look like a real morning photo: lit only by the sun and the sky through the glass wall, with corners and the far wall naturally darker, and no smudgy "crayon" look on the walls, floor or plants.

target.caption: Target: the room in Blender with the chosen daylight (sun 0.65, sky 4.5)
Target: the new wall opposite the window (painting and wall lights; the door here is the old walnut, now changed to light oak)

decisions.text: Daylight only: sun plus the sky through the glass. No chandelier, no floor lamp, no hidden ceiling light.

images.caption: Rejected: sun only (the garden turns black)
Tried: sky 1.8 (far wall too dark)
Tried: sky 4.5 with a stronger sun

decisions.text: Sun 0.65 and sky 4.5: softer sun stripes, and the far wall lit by the sky.
New wall opposite the window: light oak door, a large painting and two brass wall lights (off by day).
Light-map sizes by need, not 2K everywhere: floor 4096; rug, window wall and credenza wall 2048; other walls, ceiling, credenza, plants and curtains 1024; small things 512 or 256.
Clean the bake noise with Blender's own denoiser (OIDN) instead of the filter that smeared it into crayon blotches.
Bake one item at a time and check each before the next.
Blender's adaptive sampling was stopping dim pixels early, so more samples did nothing. Turned it off: the credenza's noise dropped about 5 times and its mottled look went away.
Re-baked the curtains and window wall with full samples (4096): noise fell from 0.18 to 0.06 and from 0.12 to 0.04. The floor (0.08) was left as it was.

images.caption: Curtains: first bake (left), full samples (right)
Window wall: first bake (left), full samples (right)

decisions.text: Found and fixed: the potted plant's leaves were being given the concrete pot material (its name 'potted_plant_01_leaves' contains 'pot'), so they were grey. Only the pot is swapped now.

Export: light maps stored as RGBM, lossless (round-trip error about 0.3%, against about 3% before); colour textures 1024 except floor and rug (2048); the plant's light as 16-bit vertex colours. The room file grew from 11 MB to 35 MB, mostly the 4096 floor map (10.5 MB): fine for the lab, can be made lighter later.
The lab now uses AgX tone mapping like the Blender renders, with day exposure 2.46 (Blender's +1.3 stops).

Light-map layout checked per group: walls, floor, rug, ceiling use 93-100% of their maps, furniture 74-87%, so no layout change. The potted plant used 1% (176,000 leaf faces), the cause of its crayon look: its light is baked into the model's points instead of an image.
